runsReviewed.name: fullstack-final
runsReviewed.notes: The YOLO process was no longer running, but run.json had completedAt=null and stopReason=null. Manual Docker/runtime acceptance passed after the run.

runsReviewed.name: fullstack-10-context
runsReviewed.notes: Used as comparison evidence for prior round chaining and generated-app runtime failure.

overall.summary: The refiner understood the project/refinement role and usually targeted the next concrete blocker. Round chaining worked for all logged handoffs. The main weaknesses were stale/misread evidence, overly broad verification prompts, and no clean terminal run status.

rounds.agentInputPrompt: Initial fullstack task plus Qwen safe file-write and MCP shell fallback guidance.
rounds.actionsTakenSummary: Created and rewrote docker-compose.yml, frontend.html, package.json, server.js, and static_server.js; ran JSON, JS, and compose checks.
rounds.commandsTestsRunSummary: 12 commands, including heredoc writes, docker compose config/build attempts, node --check, and python3 -m json.tool.
rounds.refinerRequestSummaryPreview: Original goal, current round input, safe file-write guidance, commands, file-validation feedback, errors, git status, diff, and next-prompt contract.
rounds.refinerResponseSummary: Asked for creating backend/frontend source files and then Docker runtime validation.
rounds.nextPrompt: Create backend server and frontend static files, then run Docker to validate endpoints.
rounds.tooBroadStaleRepetitiveOrIgnoredEvidence: Somewhat broad: it combined file creation, build, up, curls, and down in one round despite round 1 already exceeding the soft action budget.
rounds.followingAgentRoundFollowedPrompt: Partially. Round 2 created/reworked files but still overran the soft action budget and did not complete clean runtime verification.

rounds.agentInputPrompt: Refiner prompt to create source files and perform Docker validation.
rounds.actionsTakenSummary: Rewrote docker-compose.yml several times, created backend-code/frontend-code folders, rewrote server/static/frontend/package files, ran node checks, and copied files.
rounds.commandsTestsRunSummary: 19 commands, dominated by repeated file rewrites and syntax checks.
validationAcceptanceResults: No file-validation summary recorded for this round
rounds.refinerRequestSummaryPreview: Included original goal, prior refiner prompt, many file write commands, missing validation feedback, and acceptance-gate feedback.
rounds.refinerResponseSummary: Narrowed the next step to source-file creation plus JS/JSON/YAML validation, and explicitly deferred Docker runtime verification.
rounds.nextPrompt: Create missing source files (server.js, static_server.js, frontend.html, package.json) and validate syntax.
rounds.tooBroadStaleRepetitiveOrIgnoredEvidence: It likely hallucinated or over-stated missing files because server.js/static_server.js already existed by then. Still, it correctly prioritized validation before Docker.
rounds.followingAgentRoundFollowedPrompt: Yes. Round 3 focused on the named files, JSON/JS/YAML validation, and did not yet do full runtime acceptance.

rounds.agentInputPrompt: Refiner prompt to create/validate source files and avoid Docker runtime checks until files were valid.
rounds.actionsTakenSummary: Rewrote docker-compose.yml and core source files, validated package.json, node syntax, compose config, and frontend URL.
rounds.commandsTestsRunSummary: 16 commands, including compose config, docker compose build attempts, grep URL check, node --check, and json.tool.
rounds.refinerRequestSummaryPreview: Included valid file-validation feedback and no runtime acceptance evidence.
rounds.refinerResponseSummary: Correctly moved from syntax/config validation to Docker build/up/curl/down runtime verification.
rounds.nextPrompt: Run Docker build and verify runtime endpoints.
rounds.tooBroadStaleRepetitiveOrIgnoredEvidence: Mostly bounded and evidence-based, though the verification list still had six commands and could pressure local Qwen.
rounds.followingAgentRoundFollowedPrompt: Partially. Round 4 attempted Docker/runtime work but sprawled into many rewrites and local process experiments.

rounds.agentInputPrompt: Refiner prompt to run Docker build/up/curl/down after source validation.
rounds.agentOutputSummary: Files Created/Validated. Captured 63 actions and 63 commands.
rounds.actionsTakenSummary: Created Dockerfiles and compose build config, repeatedly rewrote compose/source files, ran local node processes, probed Docker, killed unrelated local node processes, and eventually left a buildable root app.
rounds.commandsTestsRunSummary: 63 commands. This round exceeded the soft budget badly and mixed Docker validation with unrelated process and network probing.
rounds.refinerRequestSummaryPreview: Included near-timeout diagnostics, latest files, valid compose feedback, and no captured runtime acceptance results.
rounds.refinerResponseSummary: Asked for a smaller Docker Compose build/up/curl/down repair, but incorrectly described the previous round as timed out and emitted a next prompt truncated at 'Stop after Docker'.
rounds.nextPrompt: Fix Docker Compose build and run services.
rounds.tooBroadStaleRepetitiveOrIgnoredEvidence: Stale/misread: round 4 was near timeout but not marked timed out; manual verification later passed, and the next prompt was truncated.
rounds.followingAgentRoundFollowedPrompt: No following round was logged. The process was no longer running with run.json completedAt=null and stopReason=null.

questions.didRefinerUnderstandRole: Mostly yes. It acted as a project refinement agent and generated structured next prompts.
questions.didUsePreviousAgentResult: Yes for high-level blockers, but sometimes it missed evidence from existing files and validations.
questions.didSuggestUsefulImprovements: Yes through round 3; round 4's output was less useful because it repeated a runtime repair after the project had become manually passable.
questions.didPrioritizeBlockersBeforePolish: Yes. It prioritized syntax/config/runtime blockers and avoided README/polish.
questions.didKeepPromptsBounded: Partially. Prompts were structured, but Docker prompts still encouraged too many actions for local Qwen.
questions.didRepeatStaleContext: Yes. It repeated missing-file context after files existed and described a near-timeout as a timeout.
questions.didNoticeValidationFailures: It noticed missing validation and valid file-validation feedback. There were no recorded validation command failures in this final run.
questions.didAvoidYoloStopUntilAcceptancePassed: Yes. It did not emit YOLO_STOP.
questions.didImproveProjectRoundByRound: Yes until round 4, where the agent became noisy but still left a manually passing app.
questions.whereFailed: It did not keep the agent within budget, did not prevent brittle heredoc command rendering, did not complete a clean terminal run record, and did not create README.md.

remainingQwenCodexBugsOrRisks: The final fullstack run ended with run.json completedAt=null and stopReason=null after 4 logged iterations, despite no active qwen-codex process.
The run did not classify manual acceptance evidence into finalStatus because acceptance was performed outside the run.
Qwen still often emits double-quoted shell strings around heredocs; actual file content can be repaired, but command logs remain noisy and fragile.
Refiner next prompts can be truncated when the local model hits the refiner token cap.
